summary: Task 3 deliberately ships zero automated tests, and having read the full diff (git show c0a11bc -- client/), that decision is still correct as-built: the new GarmentAddForm component contains no new pure validation logic at all — it calls Task 2's already-tested, already-exported isBlankName, isDuplicateName, and validateGarmentFields directly, unmodified, with raw string inputs (not pre-coerced via Number()||0), exactly matching Task 2's intended usage pattern. Everything else Task 3 adds (useState draft/error, an onKeyDown Enter-interception to fake form-submit semantics inside a non-<form> div, JSX wiring for the add-form and DeleteRowButton at both mode call sites) is rendering/interaction code with no independently testable pure logic — squarely the 'component/JSX wiring is manual-verification-only' category tech-spec's Testing Strategy carves out. Ran `cd client && npx vitest run` myself: 1 file, 32 tests, all passed, 616ms — identical count and file to Task 2's suite, confirming Task 3's edits caused zero regression (Task 3 touches Panel.jsx but adds no code before line 247-320 where the tested functions live, and the test file itself is untouched in this diff). Reviewed Task 3's Verify-user checklist against its own 8 acceptance criteria: 6 of 8 are directly exercised, but AC8 (price calculation with the new garment produces a correct result, no NaN/error, in both calculator modes) is not exercised by the checklist at all — it only visually confirms the field values are non-zero after switching modes, never triggers an actual price calculation. AC1 (exactly one Добавить button, not duplicated, in either mode) and AC2 (all 4 fields shown in both modes) are also only implicitly covered — the checklist opens/uses the add-form in Быстрый mode alone and never separately opens/inspects it in Продвинутый mode. These are checklist-completeness gaps, not code defects; user-spec's own broader 'How to Verify' checklist does include the price-recalculation check, so it is likely to be caught at Pre-deploy QA time, but Task 3's standalone Verify-user text does not itself guarantee that.
clean_check: DUPLICATE/DIVERGENT LOGIC CHECK (main ask): read GarmentAddForm's handleAdd end-to-end in the diff. It calls, in order: isBlankName(name) -> isDuplicateName(name, settings.garments) -> validateGarmentFields({base_minutes, complexity_coeff, quick_price}) using the raw string draft values (not Number()-coerced first, matching the task's explicit warning against the Number(value)||0 pattern). All three are imported/module-scope exports from Task 2's block (Panel.jsx:247-276), not re-implemented. Grepped the whole file for a second definition of any of these names or any local bound check (e.g. a hand-rolled `<= 0` comparison inside GarmentAddForm) — none found; the only numeric literal in the component is the `min="0"`/`step="0.01"` HTML input attributes, which are cosmetic (do not block form submission on their own) and not a second source of validation truth. Conclusion: no divergence risk exists to test, so the 'no unit tests for Task 3' decision is sound as literally nothing new-and-pure was written. REGRESSION CHECK: ran `npx vitest run` directly (not trusted from any report) inside client/ — 32/32 tests green, same file (Panel.validation.test.js) and same count as Task 2's baseline; Task 3's diff does not touch lines 1-320 of Panel.jsx (where all tested exports live) except for the two DeleteRowButton insertions and one new component block placed after line 383, none of which shadow or alter the tested functions. MANUAL-CHECKLIST-VS-AC CHECK: mapped each of Task 3's 8 ACs to the 6 bullets in its own Verify-user section line by line (task file lines 144-157 vs 91-115). AC3 (reject <=0 fields) -> bullet 3, direct match. AC4 (duplicate name rejected) -> bullet 4, direct match. AC5 (garment appears in both modes) -> bullet 2, direct match. AC6 (delete button absent on defaults, present on added row, in both modes) -> bullet 5, direct match ('in either mode' explicit). AC7 (delete persists after save+reload, both modes) -> bullet 6, direct match for the persisted-after-reload half; the 'removes it from both mode views immediately' (pre-save) half of AC7 is not separately checked, minor. AC1 (exactly one Добавить button, not duplicated/missing, in either mode) -> only bullet 1 touches this, and only in Быстрый mode; Продвинутый mode's Добавить button presence is never independently confirmed. AC2 (all 4 fields shown regardless of mode) -> only exercised by filling the form once, in Быстрый mode; the Продвинутый-mode add-form is never opened/inspected, only the already-added row's stored values are eyeballed. AC8 (adding+saving, switching mode, recalculating price, no NaN/error) -> no bullet exercises an actual price calculation; bullet 2 only checks that stored field values are 'not zero/blank' after a mode switch, which is a strictly weaker check than AC8's 'recalculating a price... produces a correct result'.

findings.location: work/pricing-panel-tweaks/tasks/3.md:143-157 (Verification Steps > User), vs Acceptance Criteria item 8 (lines 112-115)
findings.issue: AC8 explicitly requires: 'Adding then saving a garment, then switching calculator mode and recalculating a price for it, produces a correct result in both modes (no NaN, no thrown error) — confirms all 3 numeric fields were genuinely captured, not defaulted.' None of the 6 Verify-user bullets trigger an actual price calculation for the newly added garment. The closest bullet ('Switch to «Продвинутый» mode — confirm the same new garment appears with its База/Коэфф. values intact (not zero/blank)') only checks that the stored numbers are displayed and non-zero — it does not run the garment through the pricing calculator in either mode. This is precisely the bug class Decision 2 / the round-1 finding was meant to close (a garment silently getting a usable-looking but wrong/zero value for a field only shown in the other mode) — a value could display as non-blank yet still be wrong in a way that only a real calculation surfaces (e.g. a units/type mismatch that renders fine as text but breaks costing.go's quick-price path at costing.go:718-721, per the task's own Context Files pointer). user-spec's own broader 'How to Verify → Инкремент 2' checklist does include 'цена по новому изделию считается без ошибок в обоих режимах', so this will likely be exercised once Pre-deploy QA walks the full user-spec checklist — but Task 3's own standalone Verify-user text, if followed literally and in isolation, would sign off without ever calculating a price with the new garment.
findings.recommendation: Add a bullet to Task 3's Verify-user list (or explicitly rely on and reference user-spec's checklist item covering this) instructing the verifier to actually run a price calculation using the newly added garment in both Быстрый and Продвинутый modes and confirm the result is a real number, not NaN/undefined and not an error. Low cost to add since the garment is already present from the prior bullet.

findings.issue: AC1 ('exactly one Добавить button... not duplicated or missing in either mode') and AC2 ('add-form always shows all 4 fields in both modes') are only exercised in Быстрый mode by the checklist (bullet 1: 'switch to «Быстрый» mode, click Добавить... fill in a new garment'). The checklist never separately opens/inspects the Изделия add-form while in Продвинутый mode — bullet 2 only checks the already-saved row's displayed values after switching mode, not the add-form itself. Code review of the diff confirms both GarmentAddForm call sites are structurally identical (same component, same props, one per SettingsSection at lines ~1178 quick / ~1241 masterpiece), so the actual regression risk is low, but the manual checklist as written does not independently verify this for the second mode.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a short checklist step, e.g. 'While in Продвинутый mode, confirm exactly one Добавить button appears under Изделия and the form shows all 4 fields (Название, Мин. цена/шт, База/мин, Коэфф. сложности).' Not blocking — the underlying code is structurally symmetric per Decision 5's shared-component pattern, and this is a checklist thoroughness gap rather than a suspected code defect.
